## Developer Training And Support ***API Reference - REST*** Avetta provides access to select business objects through a set of RESTful APIs. In this portal you will find a list of the available endpoints with the latest information. For more information about a particular endpoint, click on it in the left pane to view a description of the endpoint and any query parameters. Also the mock testing feature will show a sample response payload. ## FAQ
What is the purpose of the APIs? APIS are meant for real time access to data that will match the data that is available in the Connect Portal. This is meant for workflows and to drive business decisions in real time or close to real time. APIS are not intended to be used for large archived data pulls or history unless the API provides it. For more information on accessing archived data contact apisupport@avetta.com.

What is the intended use or business purpose of each API end-point? - **Suppliers:** Use when you need to access supplier details and compliance by site. Has limited ability to filter by date use Connections instead if you need more specific data filters such as daily changes to Compliance or Connections. - **Audits:** Use when you only need audit data. Deprecated use Forms instead. - **Insurance:** Use when you only need specific insurance data. Deprecated use Forms instead. - **Forms:** Use for accessing all Forms, Questions, Answers. - **Flags:** Use for a list of Flags. Deprecated. Use Get Supplier Flags instead - **Files:** Use to pull a pdf file representing a form. Files must be setup properly in the hierarchy for this to work. - **Connections:** Use for accessing supplier-site connections with all relevant information (compliance, supplier details, connections) and has robust date range filtering. - **Supplier Details:** Use for accessing Supplier details and has robust date range filtering. - **Hierarchy:** Use for accessing the Client Hierarchy in Connect. Use this in conjunction with the Supplier Registration endpoint. - **SupplierRegistration:** Use to submit new Suppliers to the Connect platform. - **Contractors:** Given a supplierId, retrieve all the connections existing with the client sites and all relevant information pertaining to sub Contractors, prime Contractors, and Direct Contractors for each supplier-site connection. Corporate Hierarchy: Use for accessing the Client Hierarchy in Connect. - **Push Variance:** Not intended to be used standalone – needs to be used with new flags endpoint. Client should be pulling in flag level compliance and then use this endpoint to force the color to green without having to access the Avetta Connect UI. - **Get Supplier Flags:** Used to pull flags from all levels (site, criteria, siteVariance and criteriaVariance) - **Form Activities:** Gets all activities/comments made on a specific form from newest to oldest - **Form Status:** Gets the applicable statuses to apply for a specific form. The list of statuses would be the applicable status to set based on the current status of the form. - **Supplier Accounts:** Use this endpoint to see the linked data to other platforms using the External Id. An External Id is an identifier that usually belongs to another platform and it is being stored in our DB to link it with its Avetta Account. - **Get Connections with Compliance:** Retrieves the overall compliance status between a supplier and a client - **Client Update Supplier:** Allows you to add/update the external IDs for suppliers. External IDs are the ids used in the clients internal systems for suppliers. - **Connected Supplier Profile:** Retrieves all unique suppliers at corporate, hub or site level. - **Hierarchy:** The API retrieves the whole hierarchy for a client. - **Get External IDs:** Allows you to pull all external IDs for suppliers with the ability to filter by supplier, externalIdType and externalId. - **Delete External IDs:** Allows you to delete External IDs by supplierID or clientID. - **Get ESG Scores:** Retrieves ESG scores, ESG levels, ESG tier and ESG relative forms for the specified client and supplier. - **Create Variance Flag:** Allows users to add a “basic variance” with the status “Approved” to create a new variance flag. - **Files:** The files end point provides the FILE PATH for documents so Clients can download the document using that path - **Count endpoints:** These allow to count the number of records where this count endpoint is available (forms, suppliers, connections, etc...)

What endpoint should I request to get information about Flag Variances? To get information about Flag Variances, you should request the following endpoint: - `https://api.avetta.com/api/v2/suppliers` - `https://api.avetta.com/api/v1/connections` - `https://api.avetta.com/connect/v1/connections`

What are the general rules for usage and management of the APIs?
  • Avetta supports the latest three versions of the APIs.
  • Avetta will not make changes that cause the API interface to stop returning results if the correct request is made.
  • Avetta may add new optional parameters but will not remove any request parameters from existing APIs.
  • Avetta may add new elements to the response but will not remove any elements from existing API responses.
  • API keys that are not used for 90 days will be disabled.
  • Avetta reserves the right to disable any API keys or prevent access to APIs if there is a security or technical risk, such as excessive load on the system.
  • Avetta reserves the right to remove or replace functionality with a new version. Notification will be sent to anyone using the API to make them aware of the change.
  • For internal implementation changes that do not impact the API interface, Avetta will not notify API clients.


What are the rate limiting rules for the APIs?
  • A maximum of 20 API calls per minute per IP address is allowed for the following APIs when no id or supplierId is provided in the query parameters:
    • v1/suppliers
    • v2/suppliers
    • v1/insurance
    • v2/insurance
    • v1/forms
    • v1/audits
    • v2/audits
  • For all other cases, a maximum of 60 API calls per minute per IP address (equivalent to 1 API call per second) is allowed.
  • If the rate limit is exceeded, a 1015 HTTP status code will be returned, and the client must wait for one hour before making any further API calls.


What is the API limit for and what is the limit or maximum number of records that can be requested?
  • The API limit or maximum number of records that can be returned per individual API call is 500 by default. If more than 500 records are needed, multiple API calls must be made with different start and limit parameters. For example, if there are 10,000 records, the "count" version of the endpoint should be called first to get the total number of records available. Then, 20 calls with limit=500 should be made (updating both the start and limit parameters as needed) to iterate through all the results.
  • The default limit and maximum is 500 for all endpoints EXCEPT the forms endpoint, for which the default and maximum limit is 100.


How should the Supplier Registration endpoint be used? The Supplier Registration endpoint is meant to serve as the receiver for Supplier Registration Requests. Here are the steps to follow: - Step 1 (optional): Client accesses the hierarchy endpoint to identify the list of sites for their Account - Step 2 (required) Client submits data via Post with the required fields in the proper format to the registration API - Step 3 (required) Avetta verify that the Supplier was processed and all the data fields were imported For the Supplier registration endpoint what does status 200/400/500 indicate? Status Code 200 – OK means the Registration submission was successful. Error Code 400 or 500 means there is an error and you should check all the data and ensure all the required fields are included. For the Registration endpoint how can I test in Postman? Send the POST request using the Body tab – Raw option and post the full JSON use the example included in the documentation. For the Registration endpoint do I need to include all fields in the response? No, only the required fields For the Registration endpoint what date should I use? Any valid date in the future, recommend 2 weeks from submission date What is the date format for language, County Code? 2 digit lower case for language, 3 digit for Country Code Are there any other recommended settings? Explicitly stated UTF8 encoding and add a content type header. API Endpoints to use for Supplier Registration API testing: `http://api.avetta.com/connect/v1/registrations` and `https://api.avetta.com/v1/corporate-hierarchy/sites/` **Example test file:** ``` name: TEST primaryContact: firstName: Bob lastName: Test email: Bob.Test@test.com phone: 949.555.5555 language: en billingAddress: addressLine: 20 Test St. city: Acton state: MA postalCode: '01720' country: US reasonForRequest: API Test requestDeadline: '2021-11-16T00:00:00.00Z' requestedByClientId: 93279 requestorFullName: Joe Test requestorEmail: test@mydomain.com ```

How accurate is the information being pulled? The information pulled is live production data and is the most accurate, up to date information available.

In what level of Hierarchy are API Keys created/supported? API Keys are only supported at the Corporate node

Authenticating with Avetta APIs Avetta APIs support two authentication methods: **API Key authentication** and **OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token authentication**. Both methods pass credentials in the `Authorization` header, but the value and setup differ. API Key authentication supports all endpoints. Bearer token authentication applies to Connections, Suppliers, Forms, Supplier Flags, Register Supplier, External-IDs, Corporate Hierarchy Sites, Connected Supplier Profile, and (in a later phase) Worksite Safety APIs. ### 1. Prerequisites - Credentials issued by Avetta (API Key or OAuth Client credentials). For assistance, contact `APISupport@avetta.com`. - Access to the Avetta API Developer Portal: https://docs.connect.avetta.com/ ### 2. Method 1: API Key Authentication Include the API key on every request: - Header name: `Authorization` - Header value format: `apikey ` Example: ```curl --header 'Authorization: apikey '``` ### 3. Method 2: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Authentication OAuth uses two steps. **Step 1 — Request an access token** Token URL: `https://api.avetta.com/auth/v1/token` ```curl --location 'https://api.avetta.com/auth/v1/token' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "grant_type": "client_api_credentials", "username": "", "password": "" }' ``` **Note:** In Avetta credentials, `CLIENT_ID` maps to `accountId`, and `CLIENT_SECRET` maps to `apikey`. Example successful response: ```json { "access_token": "blah...", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600 } ``` **Step 2 — Send the token in the Authorization header** - Header: `Authorization: Bearer ` Example: ```curl --header 'Authorization: Bearer '``` ### 4. Token Expiration / Refresh (OAuth only) - Tokens expire based on `expires_in` (typically 3600 seconds). - Request a new token by repeating Step 1 before expiry. - Client API Credentials flow does not use a refresh-token endpoint. - API keys do not expire in the same way.


What is the difference between the API Key and OAuth Client API Credentials? The API Key is a unique identifier that is used to authenticate requests to the API. It is a string of 32 alphanumeric characters. The OAuth Client API Credentials are used to obtain an access token that can be used to authenticate requests to the API. They are a combination of a client ID and a client secret. The API Key is used for all endpoints except Connections, Suppliers, Forms, Supplier Flags, Register Supplier, External-IDs, Corporate Hierarchy Sites, Connected Supplier Profile, and (in a later phase) Worksite Safety APIs.

I expect many more records to be returned in my API calls, why am I only receiving a subset of data from calls to any endpoint? Our API endpoints default to a `modifiedAfter` date if the parameter is not being used. The date being used varies by endpoint so its possible that if you are expecting more data to be returned, you need to add the `modifiedAfter` parameter and use a date further back in the past than the default so that more records are returned. Please see each endpoints query parameter definitions for more details on the `modifiedAfter` parameter defaults by endpoint.

How to use API testing module? 1. Go to the developer portal, and select the endpoint you wish to test from the left navigation menu. 2. Click **try** to open the test section. 3. Click the lock icon to enter your API key. a. To use the live server, you will need your organization’s API key. To use the mock server, you can use “apikey 1234". 4. Enter all required parameters and desired query parameters. 5. Select the server type you wish to use from the dropdown. 6. Click **Execute**.

# Common Use Cases API access is available to Avetta Clients and Partners. Contact your account representative for more information on how to obtain access to the Avetta API feature.
I want to pull a full list of my Supplier’s Accounts Use the Get Supplier Accounts endpoint, with the ability to query with the following parameters: accountStatus, externalID, modifiedAfter, etc.. **Ex:** `https://api.avetta.com/connect/v1/supplier-accounts?&accountStatus=pending&modifiedAfter=2022-02-02`

I want to pull a list of my Supplier Connections Use the Get Connections endpoint to retrieve the overall flag status between a supplier and a client. This endpoint allows you to query by clientID, supplierID, status, flagColor, etc.. **Ex:** `https://api.avetta.com/client-api/v1/connections?clientId=CLIENTID&supplierId=SUPPLIERID`

I want to pull a list of Suppliers with Connections and with Compliance Use the Get Suppliers endpoint to pull a list of suppliers with connections and compliance. **Ex:** `https://api.avetta.com/client-api/v2/suppliers`

I want to pull a list of the sites within my Account’s hierarchy Pull the Corporate Hierarchy Sites endpoint to retrieve a list of your site names & site id’s Store these site names and site id’s in your CRM database if you want to use site id to filter other endpoints

I want to pull a list of Flags for each Supplier Use the Get Connections endpoint or Get Connections endpoint to pull a list of suppliers and corresponding Avetta ID or External ID Use the Get Flags endpoint to retrieve a list of all flag statuses per supplier a. Optional query parameter externalId will filter the output to a specific supplier b. Optional query parameter supplierId will filter the output to a specific supplier

I want to pull a list of Connections with Variance Use the Get Connections endpoint to retrieve a complete list of suppliers and variance statuses a. Referenced the isForced data point to track variances applied to suppliers b. FlagDetails will provide additional details regarding the variance issued

I want to pull a list of Forms, Questions, Answers Use the Get Connections endpoint or Get Connections endpoint to pull a list of suppliers and corresponding Avetta ID or External ID Use the Get Form Data endpoint to return a complete list of forms for your suppliers a. The output includes Form Name, Questions included in each form, and the supplier’s Answer to each question b. Use the query parameter categoryId to filter to a specific form for all your suppliers

I want to pull my supplier’s documents in PDF format a. Start by using the Forms endpoint to retrieve a list of your supplier’s form data. You may filter these results down by using the available parameters (supplierId, categoryId, etc.) b. Find the “href” field in the applicable Form array you want the document for c. Call the URL provided in the “href” field. Be sure to pass your API Key as a parameter d. PDF document will be returned successfully

I want to create a variance flag via API Use the Create Variance API to add a “basic variance” through API with the status “Approved” and on a site or criteria flag. This will not update the existing variance if a variance already exists on the site and criteria flag. Only one variance can be created against a RED/GREY/AMBER and can only be AMBER/RED/GREEN. 1. Use the Get Supplier flags endpoint to get supplier, site, and flag id for which you want to add the variance for. 2. Use the Create Variance endpoint with these parameters along with the color, enddate, comments and supporting file.

I want a financial risk score Avetta will provide the categoryID and analytics report of existing financial risk scores. Client will call the forms endpoint, pass the categoryID, parse for the correct questions (local risk score), all with the modified after parameter passed.

I want to pull in insurance expiration dates Avetta will provide the categoryID and analytics report of existing expiration dates. Client will call the forms endpoint, pass the categoryID, parse for the correct questions (provided by Avetta), all with the modified after parameter passed.

I want to download the COIs of my contractors Avetta will provide the categoryID. Client will call the forms endpoint, pass the categoryID, parse for the correct question. The answer to the question will be a file path. (note: multiple files can be uploaded and will be separated by ~^~). The client will need to grab the supplier ID, client ID, and the file path from the response and use it to call the files endpoint.

I want ESG score per supplier Use the Get ESG scores endpoint by passing the client ID and supplier ID to list the ESG scores.


***Block POs or Flag PO's for non-compliant suppliers*** Track supplier compliance and build into your purchasing process to ensure POs are not being issued to non-compliant suppliers, or there is some level of additional review for non-compliant suppliers
Map all suppliers from the Avetta system to the client System - The actual mapping will be done in advance of the integration. This workflow is the API call that will make that connection in the client's system. Not required if external IDs on are the site level - Get External IDs: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Account/operation/getExternalIds** - start = ?: for pagination - supplierId = ?: use this parameter if the workflow is reversed, and they have the supplier and compliance but do not know the external ID.

Pull and store all suppliers' compliance statuses in client system - Pull a complete list of our suppliers in Avetta and their current compliance status. This is a one time pull. - Connections: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Connection-Endpoint/paths/~1v1~1connections/get** - modifiedAfter = 2020-01-01. This will ensure you get all suppliers and their compliance statuses

Monitor supplier compliance status changes with nightly batch jobs - Using a delta to receive any changes in supplier compliance statuses since the last scheduled run. - Connections: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Connection-Endpoint/paths/~1v1~1connections/get** - flagModifiedAfter = yesterday: The result will be suppliers that have had a flag status change in the last day.

Monitor supplies that disconnect in nightly batch job. - Catch when a supplier disconnects from your network and mark that in client system. This will prevent a false positive for a PO. The system will need to look at the "status" value. - Connections: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Connection-Endpoint/paths/~1v1~1connections/get** - modifiedAfter = yesterday: The result will be suppliers that have had a connection status change in the last day.

Monitor suppliers that deactivate their account in nightly batch job. - Catch when a supplier deactivates their entire Avetta account and mark that in client system. This will prevent a false positive for a PO. There is a max history of 30 days for this API. - Connected Supplier Profile: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Account/operation/getSupplierProfile** - accountStatus = deactivated - modifiedAfter = yesterday

***Gather Supplier Details*** If you would like to store or track additional supplier details beyond their overall compliance status. Build business intelligence dashboards to track leading and lagging indicators.
Pull in supplier Insurance statuses in nightly batch job - Client will need to identify the exact insurance values they want to pull. TPM will then provide a questionID(s). Historical values can be provided via analytics for an initial data load. - Forms v2: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Compliance/operation/getSupplierFormsAndAnswers** - questionId = ? - modifiedAfter = yesterday

Gather specific form details in nightly batch job - Client will need to identify the exact form values they want to pull. TPM will then provide a questionID(s). Historical values can be provided via analytics for an initial data load. - Forms v2: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Compliance/operation/getSupplierFormsAndAnswers** - questionId = ? - modifiedAfter = yesterday

View individual requirement flag statuses in nightly batch job. - Client will need to identify the exact flag statuses they want. The TPM will then provide the calculationId. Historical flag values can be provided via analytics for an initial data load - Get Supplier Flags: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Compliance/operation/getSupplierFlags** - clientId = corporateId - calculationId = ? - modifiedAfter = yesterday

Get Financial Risk Data - TPM will provide exact form ID during implementation. Historical flag values can be provided via analytics for an initial data load. - Forms v2: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Compliance/operation/getSupplierFormsAndAnswers** - formId = ? - modifiedAfter = yesterday

Get ESG Data - This endpoint works differently in a sense that it will not be updated in nightly batch jobs. All scores for the supplier base will need to be pulled at a time. The cadence of pulls can be nightly, weekly, etc. - Get Supplier ESG Scores: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Compliance/operation/getSupplierEsgScores** - clientId = can be corporate to see all suppliers, or a site Id to see just a subset - start = ?: will need this for pagination since you will be getting a large amount of data back

***Automate Supplier Onboarding Process*** Automate additional business processes to automatically send newly onboarded suppliers to Avetta to have them register and begin submitting compliance data. This automated with the Blocking POs use case can ensure end to end automation through the supplier life cycle
Register Supplier - Suppliers will need to determine a trigger in their current ERP workflow. The trigger will be a yes/no for if the supplier falls into the Avetta network scope. If yes, the ERP will also need to have a mapping of the ERP sites to the Avetta sites. - Register Supplier: **https://docs.connect.avetta.com/#tag/Account/operation/register-supplier** - Name, Contact Information, and Country - reasonForRequest = an autopopulated value. Can be "Sent via API" or another predefined message that explains why this supplier was triggered. - requestDeadline = is there a date this supplier HAS to be onboarded by. - requestedByClientId = hardcoded avetta ID of the corporate node - requestedBySite = the Avetta site ID that a supplier is connecting to - requestorFullName = Representative on client side that owns supplier network. - requestorEmail = email of client representative - tags = optional values. Will need to pass the Avetta ID for specific tags. - external ID fields: ID of the supplier record in client ERP. This will automate site mapping and should be considered required.

## How to authenticate Every request to the Avetta APIs must include an `Authorization` header. You can fill it in using **one** of two methods. Pick the one that fits your integration; you do not need both.
Option A: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Option B: API Key
Best for Integrations that prefer a more secure authentication model using short-lived tokens Existing integrations already set up with an API key
Works with All endpoints All endpoints
Steps 2 steps: get a token, then send the token 1 step: send your key
Expires Yes, after expires_in seconds (typically 3600 = 1 hour) No
Header value Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN> apikey <API_KEY>
### Before you start - You need credentials from Avetta. If you don't have them, contact [APISupport@avetta.com](mailto:APISupport@avetta.com). - Your credentials are your Avetta **`accountId`** and **`apikey`**. --- ## Option A: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token This method takes two steps: first trade your credentials for a temporary access token, then send that token on each request. ### Step 1: Get an access token Send a `POST` request to `https://api.avetta.com/auth/v1/token`: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://api.avetta.com/auth/v1/token' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "grant_type": "client_api_credentials", "username": "", "password": "" }' ``` | Field | What to put in it | |---|---| | `grant_type` | Always `client_api_credentials` | | `username` | Your `accountId` | | `password` | Your `apikey` | A successful response looks like this: ```json { "access_token": "", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600 } ``` Copy the value of `access_token`. You will use it in Step 2. ### Step 2: Send the token on each request Add this header to every request: ``` Authorization: Bearer ``` **Example** ```bash curl 'https://api.avetta.com/api/v1/connections' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer ' ``` ### When the token expires - The token stops working after `expires_in` seconds (typically 3600 seconds, or 1 hour). - There is no refresh token. To keep going, repeat **Step 1** to get a new token. - Tip: request a new token shortly before the old one expires so requests don't fail. --- ## Option B: API Key Add this header to **every** request: ``` Authorization: apikey ``` Replace `` with your `apikey`. Keep the word `apikey` and the space before your key. **Example** ```bash curl 'https://api.avetta.com/api/v1/connections' \ --header 'Authorization: apikey ' ```

Our errors are listed below in the following format -> Code Error Number [Actual Message]: Description of the error.

Code 1 [Validation Failed]: An invalid API key was provided.

Code 2 [Invalid Parameters]: The start and/or limit parameters entered are not within acceptable limits.

Code 3 [Unknown Record]: The entered start parameter is beyond the total number of records available.

Code 4 [Unmapped]: Client Id that is entered is not mapped on the custom DB tables.

Code 5 [Server Error]: The system has encountered an unexpected error while processing the request.

Code 6 [ConID Error]: The requested Supplier Id is unknown under the current API key.

Code 7 [Null Data]: No audit or flag data available.

Code 8 [Invalid Format]: Provided date and time does not conform to the `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` or `yyyy-MM-dd` formats

Code 9 [Unknown file type]: Internal Server Error

Retrieves a list of multiple supplier data. By default, only suppliers that have active connections to clients will be returned in this endpoint.
* The `flags` array contains the supplier’s flag for a particular `client_id`. 
* The `client_id` field is the identifier of a specific site within your account hierarchy. 
* The `system_flag` field shows the overall flag color for a particular supplier/contractor for that `client_id`.
* The `system_flag_details` array contains the detail of your individual flaggable data and its current flag color. This provides specific detailed reasons for the current overall flag color, `system_flag` for in regards to that specific `client_id`.
* The **updated_date** field(which the `modifiedAfter` applies to) helps you quickly identify the latest updates to your suppliers. It reflects not only changes you or the supplier make but also internal system adjustments, such as updates to evaluations or categories. This means a supplier you haven't recently interacted with might still appear as "recently updated" due to these behind-the-scenes activities. It's designed to ensure you always have the most current information at your fingertips, aiding in maintaining compliance within your supply chain.
> When `supplierId` path parameter is provided, a single supplier object related to the provided Supplier Id is returned. The `start`, `limit`, and `modifiedAfter` parameters will be ignored.

get.description:
Retrieves the authenticated supplier's forms together with the question group metadata behind them - workflow definitions (including each status's `crmId`), rejection reasons and labels.

A caller may only retrieve forms belonging to the supplier they are authenticated as. If the `supplierMongoId` in the path is not the authenticated account, the request is rejected with a `403` before any data is retrieved. API keys are issued to clients rather than suppliers, so API-key callers cannot use this endpoint.

Forms hidden by visibility settings are excluded: a form is returned only if it is associated with at least one of the supplier's connected sites, and - where its question group carries a `visibleAfterDays` schedule - only once `validStartDate + visibleAfterDays` has elapsed. A form with no `validStartDate` is not returned when its question group has that setting.

`showCompleted` defaults to **true**. A form counts as completed only when `percentageComplete` is 100 **and** its workflow status has `crmId: closed`; either alone is not sufficient.

Get all the sites which are contained in a given active connection within the corporate hierarchy.

The Hierarchy consists of a collection of nodes that link every site to a hub and at the top of the Hierarchy is the root node that serves as the Corporate Account Billing Id.

Each supplier links to one or more Site nodes via a Connection.

If the API is called with only the required parameters (api key) then all sites for this client corporate account should be returned. The corporate account is determined by a lookup to identify the client linked to the apikey.

The following restrictions apply:

The client should be a corporate, which is the root node of the hierarchy.

`parentId` is a filter to show only the nodes with that selected Parent Id

Parent here means the direct parent of a site, it can be a hub or a corporate.

The reason to use the Parent Id filter is to identify a list of sites that have the same parent.

Name is a filter on the site name to show only the sites with that selected name.

Sites will only be returned only if they are linked to an active (approved)  a connection.

get.description:
Returns the complete workflow transition graph for every form within the specified work request.

Each form in the response contains a `transitions` array. A **transition group** is a single
entry in that array: it pairs one source state (`from`) with every state that form can legally
move to from there (`to`). Reading the groups in order gives you the intended
progression of the workflow from start to finish.

The `transitions` array always represents the **complete workflow state machine** — every valid
transition defined for that form's workflow type, regardless of where the form currently sits.
Use `currentStatus` to know the form's present position, and use `transitions` to understand
the full map of where it can go. A form that has already reached the terminal state will still
return the same complete transition graph as a form that has not yet started.

A workflow has exactly one terminal state — the successful outcome (e.g. "Acknowledged"). All
other states, including rejection or rework states, are non-terminal: they have their own
outgoing transitions that route the form back through the workflow so it can eventually reach
the terminal state.

**Divergent paths** — where a single state can move to more than one destination — occur when
a review transition can either advance the form (toward the terminal state) or send it back for
rework (e.g. "Rejected"). Both destinations appear in one transition group. Because the rework
destination is non-terminal, it will also appear as the `from` state of a subsequent group,
showing where the form continues after rework. You may therefore see a group whose source state
was already listed as a destination earlier — this is intentional and represents the form
re-entering the workflow after a rework transition.

**Key behaviours:**
- Transition groups are ordered by the first time each source state is encountered in the workflow, reflecting the intended workflow sequence.
- When a source state has multiple destinations, all are listed in one group — non-terminal (rework/intermediate) states first, then the terminal (final) state last.
- A rework state (e.g. "Rejected") is non-terminal: it will have its own transition group showing where the form continues, typically looping back toward the divergent transition.
- The `transitions` array is the same complete graph regardless of `currentStatus` — it never filters transitions based on where the form currently is.

**Note**: The `clientId` must match the hierarchy node where the work request was created, or one of its ancestors.

name.description: Human-readable name of the workflow status.

isFinal.description: Whether this is a terminal (final) state. A terminal state has no outgoing transitions — the form cannot move to any further state once it reaches one.
